questions.q: A particle of mass m is projected with a speed u from the ground at an angle $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ w.r.t. horizontal (x-axis). When it has reached its maximum height, it collides completely inelastically with another particle of the same mass and velocity $u\overset{^}{i} .$ The horizontal distance covered by the combined mass before reaching the ground& is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
${p}_{i} = {p}_{f}$
$mu + mucos\theta = 2mv$
$⇒ v = \dfrac{u\left(1 + cos {60}^{0}\right)}{2} = \dfrac{3}{4}u$
So horizontal range after collision $= vt$
$= v\sqrt{\dfrac{{2H}_\max}{g}}$
$= \dfrac{3}{4}u\sqrt{\dfrac{2u^{2}\sin^{2} \left({60}^{0}\right)}{2g^{2}}}$
$= \dfrac{3}{4}u^{2}\dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{4}}}{g} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}u^{2}}{8g}$

questions.q: If momentum of a body is increased by $20 %$, then its kinetic energy increases by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
A body of mass $m$, moving with momentum $p$ and kinetic energy $K$ are related as follows,
$K = \dfrac{p^{2}}{2m}$.
As the momentum of the body is increased by $20 %$, then its momentum becomes,
$\left(p + \dfrac{20}{100}p\right) = 1 . 2p$
and the mass of the body remains unchanged. So, kinetic energy is directly related to the square of momentum.

Hence, new kinetic energy $\left(K^{'}\right)$ will be,
$K^{'} = \dfrac{{\left(1 . 2p\right)}^{2}}{2m}$

$K^{'} = 1 . 44K$.

So, the percentage change in kinetic energy
$= \dfrac{K^{'} - K}{K} \times 100$
$= \dfrac{1 . 44K - K}{K} \times 100$
$= \left(1 . 44 - 1\right) \times 100$
$= 44 %$.

questions.q: An object of mass ${m}_{1}$ collides with another object of mass ${m}_{2}$, which is at rest. After the collision the objects move with equal speeds in opposite direction. The ratio of the masses ${m}_{2}: {m}_{1}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
${m}_{1}{v}_{1} = - {m}_{1}v + {m}_{2}v$

${v}_{1} = - v + \dfrac{m2}{m1}v$

\left({v}_{1} + v\right)v = \dfrac{m2}{m1}$

$e = \dfrac{2v}{v1} = 1$

$v = \dfrac{v1}{2}$

$\dfrac{{v}_{1} + {v}_{1} / 2}{{v}_{1} / 2} = \dfrac{m2}{m1}$

$3 = \dfrac{m2}{m1}$

$

questions.q: The position vector of the center of mass $\overset{→}{r}cm$ of an asymmetric uniform bar of negligible area of cross-section as shown in figure is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The position vector of center of mass& $\overset{→}{r}cm$~is given as~

$\overset{→}{r}cm = {X}_{cm}\overset{^}{x} + {Y}_{cm}\overset{^}{y}$

Where,~${X}_{cm} =x -$coordinate of center of mass and~${Y}_{cm} = y -$coordinate of center of mass

$\overset{→}{r}cm = \left(\dfrac{{m}_{1}{x}_{1} + {m}_{2}{x}_{2} + {m}_{3}{x}_{3}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2} + {m}_{3}}\right)\overset{^}{x} + \left(\dfrac{{m}_{1}{y}_{1} + {m}_{2}{y}_{2} + {m}_{3}{y}_{3}}{{m}_{1} + {m}_{2} + {m}_{3}}\right)\overset{^}{y}$

$\overset{→}{r}cm = \left[\dfrac{\left(2m\right) \times L + \left(m\right) \times 2L + m\left(\dfrac{5L}{2}\right)}{2m + m + m}\right]\overset{^}{x} + \left[\dfrac{\left(2m\right) \times L + \left(m\right) \times \dfrac{L}{2} + m \times \left(0\right)}{2m + m + m}\right]\overset{^}{y}$

$\overset{→}{r}cm = \dfrac{13L}{8}\overset{^}{x} + \dfrac{5L}{8}\overset{^}{y}$

$\overset{→}{a}A = - a\overset{^}{i}$
$\overset{→}{a}B = a\overset{^}{j}$
$\overset{→}{a}C = a\overset{^}{i}$

$\overset{→}{a}cm = \dfrac{{m}_{a}\overset{→}{a}a + {m}_{b}\overset{→}{a}b + {m}_{c}\overset{→}{a}c + {m}_{d}\overset{→}{a}d}{{m}_{a} + {m}_{b} + {m}_{c} + {m}_{d}}$
$\overset{→}{a}cm = \dfrac{- ma\overset{^}{i} + 2ma\overset{^}{j} + 3ma\overset{^}{i} - 4ma\overset{^}{j}}{10m}$

$= \dfrac{2ma\overset{^}{i} - 2ma\overset{^}{j}}{10,} = \dfrac{a}{5}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{a}{5}\overset{^}{j} = \dfrac{a}{5} \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)

questions.q: A simple pendulum of length $1m$ has a wooden bob of mass $1$ kg. It is struck by a bullet of mass ${10}^{- 2}kg$ moving with a speed of $2 \times {10}^{2}ms^{- 1}$. The bullet gets embedded into the bob. The height to which the bob rises before swinging back is. (use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Linear momentum will be conserved, therefore

$mu = \left(M + m\right)V$

$⇒ {10}^{- 2} \times 2 \times {10}^{2} ≅ 1 \times V$

$⇒ V ≅ 2ms^{- 1}$

Again from energy conservation, we get height achieved, $h = \dfrac{V2}{2g} = 0 .2 m$.

questions.q: As shown in figure. When a spherical cavity (centred at $O$ ) of radius $1$ is cut out of a uniform sphere of radius $R$ (centred at $C$ ), the centre of mass of remaining (shaded part of sphere is at $G,$ i.e., on the surface of the cavity. $R$ can be determined by the equation:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
${M}_{1} = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}ρ$
${M}_{2} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{ \left(1\right)}^{3} \left(-$ρ\right)$
${X}_{com} = $\dfrac{{M}_{1}{X}_{1} + {M}_{2}{X}_{2}}{{M}_{1} + {M}_{2}}
$⇒ $\dfrac{\left[\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}ρ\right]0 + \left[\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{\left(1\right)}^{3}\left(- ρ\right)\right]\left[R - 1\right]}{\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}ρ + \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{ \left(1\right)}^{3} \left(- ρ\right)}$$ - \left(2 - R\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{ \left(R - 1\right)}${{( R}^{3} - 1 )} = \left(2 - R\right)\left(R \ne 1\right)$
$\dfrac{\left(R - 1\right)}{\left(R - 1\right)\left(R^{2} + R + 1\right)} =2 - 1$
\left(R^{2} + R + 1\right)\left(2 - R\right) = 1$
Alternative:
${M}_{remaining} \left(2 - R\right) = {M}_{cavity} \left($1 - R\right)$
$⇒ \left($R^{3} - {1}^{3}\right) \left($2 - R\right) = {1}^{3} \left[R - 1\right]$
$⇒ \left(R^{2} + R + 1\right)\left(2 - R\right) = 1$

$

questions.q: An average force of $125N$~is applied on a machine gun firing bullets each of mass $10g$ at the speed of $250ms^{- 1}$ to keep it in position. The number of bullets fired per second by the machine gun is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the net momentum of the gun and bullet system can be written as

$F = nmv . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required number of bullets.

$\begin{cases}125 & = & n \times \dfrac{10}{1000} \times (250 ) \\ ⇒ & n = 50\end{cases}$

questions.q: Two blocks of masses $10$ kg and $30$ kg are placed on the same straight line with coordinates \left(0, 0\right)cm$ and \left(x, 0\right)cm$ respectively. The block of $10$ kg is moved on the same line through a distance of $6$ cm towards the other block. The distance through which the block of $30$ kg must be moved to keep the position of centre of mass of the system unchanged is
options: $2$ cm away from the $10$ kg block
$4$ cm away from the $10$ kg block
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Initial position of centre of mass:& ${x}_{CM} = \dfrac{10\left(0\right) + 30 \times x}{40} = \dfrac{3x}{4}$

Final position of the centre of mass:~$x^{'}CM = \dfrac{10\left(6\right) + 30 \times \left(x - y\right)}{40} = \dfrac{6 + 3\left(x - y\right)}{4}$

As position of centre of mass remains same,

${x}_{CM} = x^{'}CM ⇒ \dfrac{3x}{4} = \dfrac{6 + 3\left(x - y\right)}{4} ⇒ 3x = 6 + 3x - 3y⇒ y = 2cm$

Alternate method,~$∆ {x}_{COM} = {m}_{1} ∆ {x}_{1} + {m}_{2} ∆ {x}_{2}\left({m}_{1} + {m}_{2}\right) ⇒ 0 = 10 \times 6 + 30y ⇒ y = - 2cm$

questions.q: A player caught a cricket ball of mass $150 \mathrm{~g}$ moving at a speed of $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the catching process is completed in $0.1 \mathrm{~s}$, the magnitude of force exerted by the ball on the hand of the player is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{F}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{P}}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}-0}{0.1} \\ & =\frac{150 \times 10^{-3} \times 20}{0.1}=30 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A rubber ball is released from a height of $5m$~above the floor. It bounces back repeatedly, always rising to $\dfrac{81}{100}$ of the height through which it falls. Find the average speed of the ball. (Take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
${v}_{0} = \sqrt{2gh}$

$v = e\sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2gh}$

$⇒ e = 0 . 9$

$S = h + 2e^{2}h + 2e^{4}h + \ldots \ldots \ldots$

$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} + 2e\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} + 2e^{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} + \ldots \ldots \ldots$

${v}_{av} = \dfrac{s}{t} = 2 . 5ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two bodies are having kinetic energies in the ratio $16: 9 .$ If they have same linear momentum, the ratio of their masses respectively is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy and the momentum of a moving object are related by

$K = \dfrac{p2}{2m} . . . \left(1\right)$

Hence, the ratio of the~kinetic energies of two objects having masses~$m$~and~$m '$~can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{K}{K '}& = & \dfrac{\dfrac{p2}{2m}}{\dfrac{p2}{2m '}}\\ & = & \dfrac{m '}{m} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$$

Substitute the ratio of the kinetic energies into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the ratio of their masses.

$\begin{cases}& ⇒ & \dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{m '}{m}\\ & ⇒ & m: m ' = 9: 16\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: A particle of mass $200MeVc^{- 2}$ collides with a hydrogen atom at rest. Soon after the collision, the particle comes to rest, and the atom recoils and goes to its first excited state. The initial kinetic energy of the particle (in $eV$) is $\dfrac{N}{4} .$ The value of $N$ is: (Given the mass of the hydrogen atom to be $1GeVc^{- 2}$).........
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Given,& $M = 200MeVc^{- 2}$~and~$m = 1GeVc^{- 2}$, now use the concept of conservation of linear momentum,~$M{v}_{0} = mv ⇒ v = \dfrac{M{v}_{0}}{m} . . . \left(1\right)$.

Now use the conservation of energy,~

\dfrac{1}{2}$M \left({v}_{0}\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{2}m \left(v\right)2 + ∆ E . . \left(2\right)$, here~$∆ E = 13 . 6eV$, for the hydrogen atom in the ground state, now from equation,~ \left($1\right) \text{ and } \left(2\right)$,~\d$dfrac{1}{2}M \left({v}_{0}\right)$2 = $\dfrac{1}{4} \left($3 ∆ E \times $\dfrac{10}{8}\right)$eV = $\dfrac{N}{4},

$⇒ $\dfrac{N}{4} = \dfrac{51}{4}$eV⇒ N = 51$.

$

questions.q: A body of mass $1$ kg~collides head on elastically with a stationary body of mass $3$ kg. After collision, the smaller body reverses its direction of motion and moves with a speed of $2ms^{- 1}$. The initial speed of the smaller body before collision is ______~$ms^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let& ${u}_{1}$~be the initial speed of the smaller body before collision.~

Let~$v$~be the final speed of~the bigger body after collision.

Applying conservation of linear momentum,

$1 \times {u}_{1} + 0 = - 2 + 3v ⇒ {u}_{1} = - 2 + 3v . . . \left(1\right)$~

We know, coefficient of restitution for elastic perfectly collision is~$1$.

~$⇒ 1 = $\dfrac{v + 2}{u1}$⇒ v + 2 = {u}_{1} . . . \left(2\right)$~

Equating~ \left($1\right)and \left(2\right)$, we have

${u}_{1} = 4ms^{- 1}.

$

questions.q: In a system two particles of masses $m_1=3 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $m_2=2 \mathrm{~kg}$ are placed at certain distance from each other. The particle of mass $m_1$ is moved towards the center of mass of the system through a distance $2 \mathrm{~cm}$. In order to keep the center of mass of the system at the original position, the particle of mass $m_2$ should move towards the center of mass by the distance _____ $\mathrm{cm}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{X}_{\text {C.O.M. }}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_1 \Delta \mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{m}_2 \Delta \mathrm{x}_2}{\mathrm{~m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2} \\ & \Rightarrow 0=\frac{3 \times 2+2(-\mathrm{x})}{3+2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=3 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
